chunks.text:
Hi Ben,
I didn’t expect to get to know you this year. you were, at first, someone i encountered through the proxy of mutual friends (Jesse), a presence that showed up in certain conversations and not others. but discord-friendship has a strange way of accruing depth without anyone noticing. it’s built out of timestamps and typing indicators, out of the small decisions people make about when to speak and what to leave unsaid. over enough days, you start to recognize someone’s mind the way you’d recognize their voice. the texture of attention reveals itself.
What struck me, watching you in those spaces, was how your thinking stayed pretty legible: honest about its own shape. you’d drop an opinion without performing certainty, then let the room respond. there’s a stoic quality to that, the willingness to say what you see and then wait, without needing the validation loop to close immediately:
Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one.Marcus Aurelius, meditations 10.16
Goffman wrote about the difference between front-stage and back-stage life: the self we perform for an audience versus the back region, off-camera, where the actual craft happens1. most online spaces push everyone toward performance. but you seem to keep most of your life in the back-stage, and that’s why the little things you say land when they do. they’re largely deposits from the work already done. the signal-to-noise ratio is high because the ratio of living-to-narrating is high.
I think that’s what i respect most: the consistency that comes from someone who does the reps without needing to document them.
I’m glad we crossed paths this year. i’m also glad the respect grew the boring way, with no big moment, just the slow accumulation of “oh, this person is serious.” that’s how trust is supposed to work, i think.
looking forward to more of it.

remarque


erving goffman, the presentation of self in everyday life (1956; 1959). the front region / back region distinction is from his dramaturgical analysis of social life. goffman does not say the back stage holds a “real” self; it is where the performance is prepared and rehearsed, which is closer to what i mean by the work. ↩
